title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: A healthy Stage 2 pullback cools oscillators without breaking the 10-week and 30-week averages.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Discipline

web_blocks.html: MCX remains in a healthy Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend. On November 23, 2026, it closed at ₹3,581.60 on our facts ledger (TradingView: ₹3,565.00) [23]. That marks a controlled 5.1% dip off its ₹3,774.00 52-week high (low ₹1,921.40 ledger / ₹1,950.00 TV). A -3.97% weekly pullback cooled daily RSI from 68.90 to 55.82 (ledger 57.29) [23]. Four-hour RSI also reset from 71.86 to 50.84. That reset flipped our Stage 2 gate to CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION (BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO). Price now sits just +5.02% above its 10-week EMA (₹3,394.72) and +6.59% above its 50-day SMA (₹3,344.73) [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: MCX cooled its overbought stretch (4H RSI 50.84; +5.02% vs 10W EMA) and earned CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION. Yet 7 distribution days and our Pass 1 target trim keep fresh-cash bids at ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 while ratcheting our held stop UP to ₹3,043.24.

web_blocks.html: Broad Indian market breadth still urges selectivity. On November 23, 2026, Nifty 50 stayed in an Uptrend (narrow breadth). Only 55.2% of 500 tracked stocks sit above their 50-DMA, and 48.2% sit above their 200-DMA. The benchmark shows 3 distribution days, with 7 of 11 sectors above key averages. MCX still ranks high with an 85.0 RS score in TheWrap Stage 2 (40.6% sector breadth; ₹3,851.9 crore weekly turnover) [23]. Ledger returns stand at +15.03% over 1 month and +14.57% over 3 months (+80.05% 1-year on TV) [23]. Still, 7 ledger distribution days and silver's 14-month low on November 25 [35] kept the 4-hour chart from turning up (intraday_4h_turn: false).

MCX is not in the NSE F&O segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID) [23]. Express all exposure in cash equity only. Our options check also flags expired contract OPT-IN-002 (MCX 3300 Bull Call Spread, expired 2026-10-29, -27 DTE). Reconcile and remove it from data/options/IN.json.

Support levels stack cleanly below CMP. First come the TV 20-day SMA (₹3,499.67) and ledger 20-day SMA (₹3,458.50) [23]. Just beneath sits our institutional buy shelf at ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00. Four anchors meet inside that band: Pivot R1 (₹3,407.53), 4H 50-SMA (₹3,402.94), 10-week EMA (₹3,394.72), and 50-day SMA (₹3,344.73) [23]. Waiting for that shelf lifts fresh-cash R:R from 1.06:1 at CMP to 1.66:1.

We currently hold 25 shares in Zerodha at ₹3,494.40 average cost (+2.50% gain). Our upward-only stop ratchet raises the floor from ₹3,033.74 to ₹3,043.24 (+₹9.50 higher) [23]. This tracks the rising 30-week SMA (now ₹3,107.47 vs ₹3,094.18 previously). A decisive close below ₹3,043.24 on heavy volume breaks Stage 2 and triggers an immediate exit.

book_paragraphs: In Chapter 8, we step back from financial statements and read the refreshed November 23, 2026 chart. Two weeks ago, MCX was stretched nearly 10% above its 10-week exponential moving average with a 71.86 four-hour RSI. Since then, the stock has done exactly what a healthy Stage 2 leader is supposed to do: it pulled back 5.1% off its ₹3,774.00 52-week high to close at ₹3,581.60 on our exchange facts ledger and ₹3,565.00 on TradingView.

That orderly -3.97% one-week digestion cooled the oscillators without damaging the primary trend. Daily RSI reset from 68.90 to a balanced 55.82, 4-hour RSI cooled from 71.86 to 50.84, and weekly RSI sits at a constructive 63.07. Price now trades just +5.02% above its rising 10-week EMA (₹3,394.72) and +6.59% above its rising 50-day SMA (₹3,344.73), flipping our deterministic Stage 2 gate from extended yellow to green (CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION).

Yet two tape details keep us selective rather than aggressive. First, the broader Indian market remains an Uptrend with narrow breadth—only 55.2% of 500 tracked stocks sit above their 50-day moving average and 48.2% above their 200-day, with 3 benchmark distribution days. Second, MCX itself has logged 7 distribution days over the past 25 sessions, and its 4-hour chart has not yet triggered an upside turn as silver's drop to a 14-month low on November 25 weighed on short-term sentiment.

Look at the exact geometry of our support shelf. Between ₹3,343.80 and ₹3,460.00, four institutional moving averages and pivots stack almost on top of each other: the ledger 20-day SMA at ₹3,458.50, Pivot R1 at ₹3,407.53, the 4-hour 50-SMA at ₹3,402.94, the 10-week EMA at ₹3,394.72, and the 50-day SMA at ₹3,344.73. When four timeframes converge inside a ₹116 band, patient buyers get a clean shelf to lean against.

Because our Zerodha account now holds 25 shares of MCX at ₹3,494.40 average cost (+2.50% gain), we also enforce our upward-only stop-loss ratchet. As the 30-week SMA climbed from ₹3,094.18 to ₹3,107.47, our structural invalidation floor ratchets UP from ₹3,033.74 to ₹3,043.24. We never lower a stop to accommodate a dip—and here, the rising trend allows us to tighten protection upward.

Finally, remember that MCX is not part of the NSE F&O segment, so all positioning remains pure cash equity, and the expired October 29, 2026 ledger item OPT-IN-002 (-27 DTE) should be removed from data/options/IN.json.

Let us walk through the exact volume and volatility footprint behind this pullback so you know what healthy digestion looks like versus genuine distribution. On the November 23 exchange facts ledger, MCX traded 20.21 lakh shares—roughly 0.82 times its 20-day average volume—while on TradingView its 30-day volume ratio sat near 1.09 times, with Bollinger Band width contracting to 19.64% and 14-day Average True Range holding steady at ₹128.45, or about 3.6% of the share price. Meanwhile, MCX's 85.0 Relative Strength percentile in TheWrap Stage 2 and its ₹3,851.9 crore average weekly turnover confirm deep institutional liquidity inside an Investment Banks and Brokers industry group where 40.6% of constituents remain in Stage 2.

What would turn this watchful pullback into a confirmed add-on trigger? Watch the 4-hour and daily tape together as price approaches ₹3,343.80 to ₹3,460.00. Right now, the 4-hour chart sits just shy of its 20-EMA at ₹3,566.13, with its 50-SMA waiting directly beneath at ₹3,402.94—virtually overlapping the 10-week EMA at ₹3,394.72 and Pivot R1 at ₹3,407.53. A calm, below-average-volume dip into that ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 shelf followed by a decisive reversal day back above the 4-hour 20-EMA would confirm institutional bids defending the trend. Conversely, a heavy-volume slice through ₹3,343 toward the 30-week SMA at ₹3,107.47 keeps fresh capital firmly in cash while our ₹3,043.24 hard stop protects the existing 25 shares.

book_subsections.title: Why Technical Green Does Not Override Valuation Asymmetry
paragraphs: Notice the subtle tension between our technical screen and our portfolio action. Technically, MCX at ₹3,565–₹3,581 passes the Stage 2 non-extended check (+5.02% above its 10-week EMA, RSI 55.82). That confirms we should confidently HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP on our existing 25 shares rather than selling into a normal 5% pullback.

For fresh capital, however, passing a technical screen is necessary—not sufficient. With our refreshed ₹4,150 Base Target and ₹3,043.24 ratcheted stop, buying additional shares at ₹3,581.60 offers only ₹568.40 of upside against ₹538.36 of stop risk—a 1.06-to-1 ratio that fails our 1.50-to-1 institutional hurdle.

Waiting for just a 3.4% dip into ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 flips the math completely: upside expands to ₹690.00 (+19.9%), stop risk shrinks to ₹416.76 (-12.0%), and reward-to-risk clears 1.66-to-1. Keep your existing 25 shares working, trail your stop to ₹3,043.24, and let the market bring the add-on tranche to ₹3,460.00.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Trail Stops Upward, Never Downward
book_callouts.text: When a Stage 2 leader's 30-week moving average rises from ₹3,094 to ₹3,107, ratcheting your stop upward from ₹3,033.74 to ₹3,043.24 locks in discipline. You hold your starter shares cleanly through normal volatility while refusing to chase fresh capital below a 1.5:1 risk-reward ratio.
